title: FlattenOptions.gAvroParity() does not reproduce GAvroSchemaFlattener's names for any field containing an underscore
rationale: FlattenOptions' javadoc states that its defaults reproduce the widely-used GAvroSchemaFlattener conventions so a caller migrating from that flattener starts at parity and changes only what they mean to change. That is false. GAvroSchemaFlattener.buildPath calls FlattenedPath.escapeSegment on every segment; the enriched defaults under the FAIL policy escape nothing. A published parity claim that does not hold is exactly what this corpus is for, and no test in the repository compared the two.
catchesBugClass: A factory method whose NAME is a claim the code does not keep. Also catches either flattener changing its default separator behaviour, and any future decision to make the enriched defaults actually escape, which would flip this row and correctly force a manifest rewrite.
cannotCatch: It cannot say which of the two is right, and it cannot tell a reader whether the parity claim was aspirational or a regression, because there is no history in the corpus. It measures names only, not the type mapping GAvro also produces.

predicted.detail: The enriched arm emits unescaped names; the GAvro arm escapes every segment, so the two disagree on both underscore-bearing columns.

configDescription: assert ENRICHED_KEYSET vs GAVRO_SCHEMA_FLATTENER, default FlattenOptions
